intro: You have come to Mor Hananyo Monastery, a monastery and church in Mardin province, founded in 493. For centuries it was the seat of the Syriac Orthodox patriarchate. And beneath it lies something even older: a vaulted room that survives from a sun temple that stood here before the monastery.
history: The monastery was founded in 493, and from the twelfth century until 1932 it was the seat of the Syriac Orthodox patriarchate. Its name carries a lovely story: saffron, it is said, was mixed into its mortar. Beneath the buildings lies a vaulted room whose blocks were laid without mortar. It is far older than the monastery and belongs to the sun temple that stood here.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Patriarchal rooms, the Sun temple chamber, the Main church and the Patriarchal throne.
facts: Did you know? The ceiling of the underground chamber is built of interlocked blocks laid without any mortar, the best preserved example of the technique in the region, and this vaulted room is far older than the monastery itself. The monastery was the seat of the Syriac Orthodox patriarchate for centuries, until it moved to Damascus in 1932.
outro: This brings our tour of Mor Hananyo Monastery to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
